verdict.rationale: Vercel's Limits page documents a full table of API rate limits (per-action limits, durations, scopes) and platform caps such as Concurrent Deployments (1 / up to 500) and builds per hour. It also documents per-plan Vercel Functions limits: maximum duration, memory and CPU. The REST API documents X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers, so a developer can plan for scale against published numbers. Missing for 10: no explicit per-function concurrency cap in the evidence (Fluid compute is only described as scaling concurrency), and no independent or hands-on corroboration of the published limits.

support.subject: As a developer, I know the documented rate limits and concurrency caps for APIs and functions so I can plan for scale

citations.quote: Rate limits are hard limits that apply to the platform when performing actions that require a response from our API.
Rate limits are specified via response headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and X-RateLimit-Reset
Memory and CPU: 2 GB / 1 vCPU default and max [Hobby] / 2 GB / 1 vCPU default, up to 4 GB / 2 vCPU max [Pro and Enterprise]
